questions.q: Why is Tableau Public the right publishing choice for the Board's deck specifically?
options: It automatically formats currency fields for non-technical audiences
The Board includes external members without Tableau Desktop licenses or internal network access, and Tableau Public offers a browser-accessible link requiring neither
It's the only option that supports LOD expressions
It's required for any workbook that uses a FIXED calculation
questions.explain: Tableau Public is Tableau's free, web-hosted option built exactly for an audience outside the company's own infrastructure and licensing.

questions.q: Why can't this workbook keep its Live connection to the dw.* warehouse once published to Tableau Public?
options: The warehouse itself blocks all external connections permanently
Tableau Public cannot maintain a live connection to a private, on-premises SQL Server database — there's no (and shouldn't be a) network path from the public internet to it
Live connections only work with Microsoft SQL Server, not Tableau Public
Live connections are disabled in all versions of Tableau
questions.explain: Publishing to Tableau Public requires converting the data source to an Extract first, since a live link to a private internal database from the public internet isn't possible or appropriate.

questions.q: Does converting to an Extract compromise the correctness of the numbers in the published Board deck?
options: Yes, because extracts recalculate all LOD expressions differently
No — the extract is a snapshot of the exact same correct warehouse data taken at one point in time; what's lost is automatic refresh, not correctness
No, but only if the extract is refreshed every hour
Yes, extracts always introduce rounding errors
questions.explain: The underlying figures are exactly as correct as they were the moment the extract was taken — only the live, automatic refresh is lost, not the data's accuracy.

questions.q: What manual step keeps the published Tableau Public deck current for each new QBR cycle?
options: Rebuilding the entire workbook from scratch every quarter
Refreshing the Extract and republishing the workbook before each new cycle
Nothing — Tableau Public automatically refreshes extracts nightly
Switching the connection back to Live once published
questions.explain: Extract Data → Refresh, followed by republishing, is the manual step required to keep the public deck current before each QBR.

questions.q: How does Tableau Public's publishing approach compare to Power BI's from Lesson 15?
options: Power BI stays live via a gateway with automatic nightly refresh for internal Executives; Tableau Public uses a manually refreshed extract for a broader, external-accessible audience
Tableau Public requires a gateway, while Power BI does not
Power BI cannot be published at all, unlike Tableau
They are functionally identical in every respect
questions.explain: Each publishing approach fits its actual audience's constraints — an internal, licensed audience for Power BI's live gateway refresh, and a broader, unlicensed audience for Tableau Public's extract-based approach.
